sentences.text: Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal Ms. Indu Pande, learned counsel for the appellant prays for withdrawal of I.A. No.13351/2024 as with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the case is taken up for final disposal at motion stage.

The appellant is aggrieved of the judgment dated 09.12.2022 passed by learned Special Judge under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO) in Special Case No. ATR 26/2019 whereby the appellant has been convicted for offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 (1)
of the IPC and Sections 3/4 of the POCSO Act and so also under Section 3 (2)
(v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and sentenced to undergo RI for 1 year (fine Rs.500), 1 years (fine Rs.500), ten years (Rs.1,000/-), and RI for Life (fine Rs.1,000/-), respectively NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17340 2 CRA-12456-2022 with default stipulation.

sentences.text: 2. It is submitted by Ms. Pande that it is a case of consensual relationship.
The prosecutrix has admitted her letters contained in Exhibits D-1 to D-12 written by her to the appellant.
She also admitted her photographs contained in Exhibits D-13 to D-21 to be that of the appellant and herself.
It is further submitted that the age of the prosecutrix is doubtful.

Ms. Pande also submits that Anand Meena vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121315300/
1 prosecution has failed to prove that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of the incident.

sentences.text:
It has not brought 10th Class marksheet on record despite the fact that the prosecutrix herself admitted that at the time of the incident she was a student of Class 12.
3.
Reading from the evidence of PW-14 (Shri Ramswaroop Vaktiya), a teacher of the concerned School, it is mentioned that he was working as incharge Principal of the Government Higher Secondary School.
It is admitted by him that the date of birth of the prosecutrix was recorded as 09.03.2002 at the instance of her parents.
She was admitted in school on 11.07.2007 vide Exhibit P-20-C.
However, he has admitted in cross- examination that there is no documentary evidence in support of her date of birth.
He has admitted that the date of birth was given by the parents.
Thus, it is submitted that mere positivity of the DNA report is not a sufficient circumstance to hold the appellant guilty.
It is further submitted that parents of the prosecutrix admitted that they had made engagement of the prosecutrix with one Shri Arvind before this incident.
Thus, it is submitted that there is presumption of majority of the prosecutrix.
In view of such submissions, prayer is made for acquittal of the appellant.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17340 3 CRA-12456-2022 4.

Shri Nitin Gupta, learned public prosecutor submits that since DNA report is positive, violation of privacy of the prosecutrix is proved beyond reasonable doubt and, therefore, the judgment of the trial Court may be maintained.

5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, it is evident that parents of the prosecutrix as well as grandfather of the prosecutrix admitted that the prosecutrix are five brothers and sisters i.e. three sisters and two brothers, and age of none of them is mentioned.

Parents have not given date of birth of any of their children nor they have mentioned the order in which their children were born.
6. As far as school teacher (PW-14) is concerned, he has admitted that date of birth is recorded as was given by the parents of the prosecutrix.
There is an admission that no documentary evidence in support of date of birth was brought on record.
Parents of the prosecutrix - (PW-2) and (PW-3) have admitted that they do not know date of birth of any of their children.

7. Thus, this aspect is required to be considered in the light of the judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of Birad Mal Singhvi v. Ananad Purohit 1988 SC 1796, wherein Hon'ble the Supreme Court has held that Section 35 of the Indian Evidence Act lays down that entry in any public, official book,
register, record stating a fact in issue or relevant fact and made by a public servant in the discharge of his official duty specially enjoined by the law of the country is itself the relevant fact.

entities.text: Birad Mal Singhvi v. Ananad Purohit 1988 SC 1796
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
To render a document admissible under Section 35, three conditions must be satisfied, firstly, entry that is relied o n m u s t b e o n e i n a p u b l i c o r o t h e r o f f i c i a l b o o k , N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-JBP:17340 4 CRA-12456-2022 register or record; secondly, it must be an entry stating a fact in issue or relevant fact; and thirdly, it must be made by a public servant in discharge of his official duty, or any other person in performance of a duty specially enjoined by law.

An entry relating to date of birth made in the school register is relevant and admissible under Section 35 of Anand Meena vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121315300/
2 the Act but the entry regarding the age of a person in a school register is of not much evidentiary value to prove the age of the person in the absence of the material on which the age was recorded.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Thus, it is evident that there is no material brought on record on the basis of which date of birth of the prosecutrix was recorded.
Thus, scholar register alone is not sufficient to accept the date of birth of the prosecutrix in absence of the material on the basis of which it is recorded.
Parents admitted that they do not know date of birth of any of their children.
They do not know even the exact age of any of the children.
In view such facts, when evidence of PW-14 school teacher is taken into consideration, the prosecution has failed to prove the age of the prosecutrix.

9. It has also come on record that during her relationship with the appellant and at the time when they were moving together from hometown to other places like Indore, etc. she had sufficient opportunity to narrate her woes if she was forcefully abducted or her privacy was violated against her will.
But the contrary facts are available on record.
Therefore, aspect of her kidnapping does not exist.
There is admission of the victim that she was in love affair with the appellant.
She has also admitted that her engagement was made with one Shri Arvind prior to the incident.
That means she was adult at NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17340 5 CRA-12456-2022 the time of the incident.

Therefore, when these aspects are taken into consideration and also looking the affection of the prosecutrix with the appellant as reflected from Exhibit D-1 to D-21, this Court is of the opinion that since the prosecution has failed to prove that the prosecutrix was minor and not attained the age of adulthood, and, therefore, conviction of the appellant under Sections 363, 366,
376 (1) of the IPC and Sections 3/4 of the POCSO Act and so also under Section 3 (2) (v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.
10.

sentences.text: In the result, the appeal is allowed.
The impugned judgment dated 09.12.2022 is set aside.
The appellant is in custody, he be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.
The record of the trial Court be sent back.
The case property be disposed of in terms of the judgment of the trial Court.
